PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes GymnasiumDriver, but that bridge cannot publish this wrapper's contract. The wrapper's Dict action space keys already start with 'action.' (gym_wrapper.py:95-98) and unmap_action reads those exact keys (gym_wrapper.py:121-140). The gymnasium bridge prefixes every Dict key with 'action.' when it derives limits, so it produces the path 'action.action.gripper_close'; 'python3 -m mhs.driver reference' failed with 'limit path action.action.gripper_close does not resolve in the input schema'. The package is therefore a direct Driver over the card's first entry symbol, robocasa.wrappers.gym_wrapper:RoboCasaGymEnv. The step input names the five fields without the upstream prefix and the driver restores 'action.<field>' before the native step; no upstream syntax was changed and the SDK was not edited. Minimal repro for the SDK: any GymnasiumDriver whose fake Dict action space has a dotted key such as 'action.x' fails the reference the same way; escaping or nesting dotted Dict keys when building the derived limit paths would fix it.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.world.step.v1 takes ticks plus the five wrapper action fields (gripper_close length 1, end_effector_position 3, end_effector_rotation 3, base_motion 4, control_mode 1), every element limited to -1..1 from gym_wrapper.py:97-98; a step applies the same action for each tick and returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated, tick and state_hash. cap.world.reset.v1 calls the wrapper's reset(seed, options): a seed replaces the inner numpy generator (gym_wrapper.py:342-346) and options is accepted but ignored by the wrapper. cap.world.seed.v1 records the seed the next reset will use; the wrapper has no separate seed method, so it makes no native call, which is why G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for seed is the only warning. The @estop closes the wrapper (close, gym_wrapper.py:392-393) and the @reset hook reopens it at the recorded seed, so the safe state is a stopped, still readable simulation.

RISK: R1 (simulation stepping), not R0: every step advances a simulated robot arm and mobile base, which MHS/spec/04-safety.md classifies as simulation stepping. There is no hardware backend, no physical effect outside the process and no independent hardware e-stop to cite; none is claimed. The card's risk_floor R0 is met.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo, robosuite, gymnasium and the roughly 10GB kitchen assets (README.md:65) are not installed and were not run; the fake backend is a pure Python kinematic stand-in with placeholder state values and 2x2x3 camera frames (the upstream observation space declares 256x256x3, gym_wrapper.py:244-250), reward 0.0 and done False for the base Kitchen success test (kitchen.py:1542-1551), and it was never compared with the upstream environment. The concrete PickPlaceCounterToCabinet success test, reward, horizon behaviour, contacts, actuators, sensors and real camera are NOT COVERED. No sim or hardware backend is declared; the real wrapper path would need robocasa imported, robosuite, MuJoCo 3.3.1 (setup.py:21) and the kitchen assets. The README's split='pretrain' constructor option (README.md:80) is not exposed by this fake-only driver. The fake's state lengths and initial values are placeholders.

WARNINGS: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 only. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No extensions were used, so there are no catalogue_requests. No site-limits.example.json is needed because the driver declares no operator-required limit. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') and adds seven cases (action envelope refusals, step advance and placeholder motion, seeded reset repeat, seed for the next reset, reset options accepted and ignored, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass.
